title: Hearing the teenage Art Tatum at the blind school in Columbus
summary: A pianist took him to a Columbus blind school to hear a 14 or 15-year-old he calls the greatest piano player in the world, who played as well with either hand.

venues.name: Ohio State School for the Blind

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Yeah, tell me the story about how you met Tatum in your first time.
Oh, well, it was the first band I was playing -- one of the first bands I ever played with. It was in Columbus, Ohio. It wasn't the very first one, but one of the first ones.

And the piano player came to me one day -- said, Man, why don't you go with me and hear the goodest piano player in the world. So I -- you know -- went along with him. I didn't know where we was going, but wound up we went to a blind school.
In Columbus, and he introduced me to this skinny guy. He said this is the greatest piano player in the world. And this kid was around 15 -- 14 or 15 years old you know.
-- And he sat down at the piano and really he convinced me.

Yeah. He played so much -- he played the same thing with his left hand as he did with his right hand. You know all that fast -- you do it -- he could play it one handed -- didn't need two hands. Either hand -- don't make no difference.
That's how I first met him.
But he was still in -- he was still in school then --
Yeah, he was going to the blind school.
He was going to blind school. I don't know -- I think he had made a couple of concert tours then.
He was a genius you know.
So you heard about him -- actually heard him playing much sooner than --
